about: Real tennis movement for the WebXR tennis game: SMPL-X motion.json clips (AGENTS.md, Dream bundle; avatars/README.md, motion.json and skinning) captured with GVHMR (the copy bundled in 4DAnyone) from freely licensed Pexels videos, cleaned by apps/webxr/scripts/tennis_motion/build.py.
coordinates: Metres, +Y up, soles on y = 0, right-handed player, the opponent toward -Z. Clips start facing -Z with the pelvis over x = z = 0 (loops: centred over the cycle), except: serve is turned so the racket head travels toward -Z at contact (it starts side-on, left shoulder to the net, about 45 degrees), and celebrate faces -Z during its V.

body.retarget: Joint rotations play on any SMPL-X avatar as they are. For an avatar whose rest skeleton has pelvis J0' and leg length L' (avatars/lucid_avatars/retarget.py leg_length): s = L' / legLength; root_t' = s * (root_t + restPelvis) - J0'; scale rootVelocity and contact positions by s too.

frames: frames[i] = {root_t, root_q [x,y,z,w], pose: 55 x axis-angle}, applied exactly as SMPL-X applies transl, global_orient and the joint rotations; pose[0] is zero. Right hand holds a racket grip (hand_poses fist at 0.9), left hand relaxed.
events: Frame numbers (0-based, at fps). contact: racket meets ball. serve: tossRelease (ball leaves the left hand), tossPeak (ball at its highest), contact.
contactPose: For strokes (contactFrame = events.contact), the racket hand at the contact frame in the clip's space: rightWrist (the joint), rightWristQuat (its world rotation, [x,y,z,w]), velocities in m/s, and an estimated racket: racketHead = grip + 0.50 m along racketDir, with racketDir fixed in the hand at 45 degrees between the fingers and the thumb (a shake-hands grip; GVHMR tracks neither fingers nor the racket, so treat it as a starting point and line the ball up with racketHead).
loops: loop: true clips end one frame before they repeat (frame N-1 flows into frame 0). Travel loops (run, shuffles) are in place: root_t x/z are 0 and rootVelocity[i] = [vx, vz] m/s is the per-frame horizontal velocity of the footage (mean + surge); position += rootVelocity[i] * scale * dt. meanVelocity is its average and speed its length (m/s).
